chunks: Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā al-ʿUbaydī narrated from al-Ḥasan ibn Rāshid, who said:

I asked al-ʿAskarī عليه السلام about a man who bequeathed one-third of his estate after his death and said: “My one-third after my death is to be divided among my male and female mawālī.” While his father also had mawālī, are his father’s mawālī included in his bequest on the basis that they are called his mawālī, or are they not included?
So he عليه السلام wrote: “They are not included.”

key_terms.أَوْصَى: he made a bequest or testamentary instruction
key_terms.بَعْدَ مَوْتِهِ: to take effect after his death
key_terms.بِثُلُثِهِ: with one-third of his estate or property
key_terms.مَوَالِيَّ: my male mawālī, meaning those legally affiliated as his male servants or dependents in context
key_terms.مَوْلَيَاتِي: my female mawālī, meaning those legally affiliated as his female servants or dependents in context

ai.seo_question: Are a father’s servants included when a man bequeaths part of his estate to his own mawālī?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning the interpretation of a bequest of one-third of an estate. It clarifies that when a man assigns that share to his own male and female mawālī, the mawālī of his father are not included in that wording.
